slides.title: Last week we made three promises. Here is where each one stands.
bullets: Test more model designs. Done. Five models tested. None of them finds Folded Lens.
Give rare tags more weight during training. Done. Folded Lens catches went from 2 of 36 to 17 of 36.
Find the best decision cut-off for Folded Lens. Done. We tested every cut. The weighted model works at any cut, so we keep 0.5.
This deck shows the numbers behind each answer.
slides.notes: Open with the three promises. Each maps to one slide. Total deck is 6 slides plus the closing slide.

slides.title: Promises vs results
slides.subtitle: One row per promise. The slide number shows where the evidence sits.

rows: All five designs miss Folded Lens
Weight rare tags higher in training
Folded Lens catches: 2 of 36 up to 17 of 36
Cut does not matter on the weighted model. We keep 0.5.

slides.title: Model design test: five designs, none finds Folded Lens
slides.subtitle: Same data, same training settings. One model trained at a time.
bullets: Every bigger model scores lower overall than the standard one. All five miss all 36 Folded Lens test pictures.
The scores barely differ between models. Running the same model twice moves the balance score by 0.037, which is more than the gaps in this table.
The four bigger models give every Folded Lens picture a negative score. No decision cut can recover them.
Conclusion: the model design is not the problem. The data is.
slides.notes: Overall score = macro AUPRC. Balance score = macro F1. Say both names once, then use the plain names.

slides.title: Weight change: Folded Lens catches went from 6% to 47%
slides.subtitle: One change on the standard model. A missed Folded Lens now counts 18 times more during training.

rows: Of our flags, how many were right

bullets: The model did not learn to see a folded lens. We made misses cost 18 times more, so the model now speaks up more often.
That is why we call this a patch. The real fix is more Folded Lens examples in the data.
No other tag got worse. Multiple Lenses and Missing Primary Package stayed perfect. Missing Lens and Cavity Off Center improved.
The balance gain of 0.084 is more than twice the 0.037 that a repeat run moves on its own. The weight change caused this, not run-to-run luck.
slides.notes: Expect the question: why did the number of false alarms rise? Answer: a model told to speak up more also speaks up when unsure. The cut-off slide shows the trade in numbers.

slides.title: Weight change, tag by tag: only Folded Lens was weak, and it moved
slides.subtitle: Pictures caught at the 0.5 cut, before (grey) vs after the weight change (green)

charts.title: Pictures caught of the total present

bullets: Four tags were already at or near perfect and stayed there. The weight change did not trade them away.
Folded Lens is the one bar that moves: 2 of 36 up to 17 of 36.
This is the picture to remember from the weight experiment.
slides.notes: Chart data source: test_predictions dumps of the 2026-09-28 baseline run and the 2026-10-05 weighted run, counted at threshold 0.5. Numbers match slide 4's table.

slides.title: Decision cut test: the weighted model works at any cut
slides.subtitle: We moved the Folded Lens cut from 0.5 down to 0.05. No retraining. Scores already saved.
bullets: Moving the cut changes almost nothing on the weighted model: one more catch, two more false alarms, across the whole range.
The same test on the unweighted model matters a lot: catches climb from 2 to 12 as the cut drops, but the best balance score reaches only 0.46 against our 0.52.
So weighting beats tuning. We keep the standard 0.5 cut: moving to 0.2 buys one picture at the cost of one more false alarm.
The limit stays the same either way. Folded Lens has 178 examples in our data and all of them sit inside Multiple Lenses.
slides.notes: Method note if asked: the sweep reads the 677-picture test set. A quoted operating threshold for production should come from a separate validation slice. We will cut one before fixing a production threshold.

slides.title: Decision cut test: the weighted model wins at every cut
slides.subtitle: Folded Lens balance score (F1) as the cut moves from 0.5 down to 0.05

charts.title: Folded Lens F1 by decision cut-off

bullets: The grey line climbs as the cut drops, but never reaches the green line. Weighting beats tuning at every single cut.
The green line is nearly flat: the weighted model does not need a tuned cut. The default 0.5 works.
Best unweighted score anywhere on this chart: 0.46. Weighted model at the default cut: 0.51.
slides.notes: Curve source: threshold sweep on saved score dumps, both runs, computed 2026-10-06. The x axis is the decision cut-off from 0.5 (left, default) to 0.05 (right, most permissive).

slides.title: Where this leaves us
bullets: Model design: settled. The standard ResNet 50 stays. Bigger models do not help.
Training loss: weighted. Folded Lens catch rate is 47% and rising with more data. This is the bridge until better annotations arrive.
Decision cut: tested. 0.5 stays. The weighted model is stable across cuts.
Next: the same weight change on the other four models, and the open client question on new Folded Lens examples.
Around 5,000 new annotated images are expected from the client. Those are the real fix for rare tags.
slides.notes: Internal, unconfirmed in writing: client said about 5,000 annotated images are coming. Back office runs the full multi-class multi-label analysis per the URS. Edge device only needs pass or fail. Client is consolidating the bubble class. All verbal from the meeting.
